podcast.body: Released in 1978, several months after the *Bat Out of Hell* album, this song is a theatrical performance blending drama and rock. Its theme of teenage lust depicts a boy attempting to persuade a girl to have sex in a car. The duet features Ellen Foley and Meat Loaf, with a narrative intro ("I remember every little thing...") and a unique baseball play-by-play by Yankee Legend Phil Rizzuto during the climax of the seduction attempt. Foley's character then interjects, demanding to know if he will love her forever before she goes further. After some evasion ("Let me sleep on it"), he agrees to everlasting love once she assents to "go all the way tonight," followed by a section of regret from the male character. The song "snuck into the top 40 at number 39" on Billboard, a surprising but understandable chart position given the disco era's radio landscape. "Paradise by the Dashboard Light is every bit a theatrical performance, and it's as much drama as it is rock."

This 7-minute and 56-second song faced significant challenges when released as a 7-inch single in 1977, due to the need to make it "pop" through AM radio and fit its considerable length onto one side of the record. To achieve this, the grooves on the 7-inch record had to be cut incredibly close together and narrower, which regrettably sacrificed the amount of bass that could be stored. "One of the absolute worst offenders was the 1977 Meat Love hit Paradise by the dashboard light."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
